cf.title: Reducing relcache memory usage: deduping index shapes

input.subject: Reducing relcache memory usage: deduping index shapes

verdict_reasoning: The goal has shown demand and no objection survived at levels 1a or 1b. Two fixable level 2 points remain. replication-ondisk-1: message #9 accepts the dangling fn_mcxt problem in shared rd_supportinfo, and no changelist through v5 says it is fixed. maintenance-fit-2: the 0003 commit message admits extra load work, and the thread has only memory numbers. Both need an answer from the author and a committer who knows relcache and fmgr.

brief.title: Deduplicate opclass-derived index fields in the relcache, add a System memory context
brief.problem: Each index relcache entry allocates its own opclass-derived arrays, including nkeyatts * amsupport FmgrInfos, even when many indexes share the same key definition. Each entry also gets its own aset context with large fixed overhead. This costs a lot of backend memory with many indexes, for example partitioned tables or schemas with hundreds of thousands of indexes.
brief.proposed_design: A per-backend "Relation shape cache" shares one set of rd_opfamily, rd_opcintype, rd_support and rd_supportinfo among indexes with the same AM, number of key attributes, opclasses and opclass options. A new SystemContext type, by Andres Freund and first named Proxy, sends every palloc to malloc and has a small header. The relcache uses it for "index info" and "index shape" contexts.
user_visible_surface: New memory context type SystemContext (systemctx.c), shown as a new type in pg_backend_memory_contexts.
New C API for creating System contexts, available to extensions.
New "Relation shape cache" context and per-shape "index shape" contexts under CacheMemoryContext.
rd_opfamily, rd_opcintype and rd_support in RelationData become const, and their memory is shared across indexes; extensions that write to them break.
fmgr.h and c.h change; the material does not say how.
author_claims: On a freshly initdb'ed catalog, "index info" memory drops from about 288 kB to about 45 kB with the full patchset.
An average "index info" context uses about 329 bytes, against 2086 bytes on master.
A reviewer measured 776 MiB to 633 MiB of relcache memory on a schema with about 39,000 tables and 148,000 indexes.
Loading index relcache entries costs slightly more work, which the author calls a worthy trade-off.
The relcache code changes rarely, so the patch could be applied to older versions for testing.
brief.thread_state: David Rowley reviewed the System context several times and sent a fixup on v4; his choice between two fixes for the realloc failure path is open. Chao Li's report of shared rd_supportinfo keeping a dangling fn_mcxt was acknowledged, and no later changelist says it was fixed.
unclear: Whether v5 fixes the fn_mcxt and fn_extra lifetime problem in shared rd_supportinfo.
No numbers show the extra CPU cost of loading index relcache entries.
The proposal does not say when shape cache entries are freed under heavy relcache invalidation.
The author's question about naming "index shape" contexts got no answer.
The deduplication patch has had less review than the System context patch.

prior_attempts.title: Separate memory contexts for relcache and catcache
prior_attempts.quote: Andres's concern, IIUC, is that the additional memory contexts will cause additional fragmentation.
prior_attempts.reason: Andres Freund's messages are not shown, but Jeff Davis reports Andres's concern that the extra contexts add memory fragmentation in each backend. Jeff saw rough consensus only for CatCacheContext and RelCacheContext, and the thread was still looking for ways to reduce the fragmentation. Rahila Syed and Ashutosh Bapat found little value in PlanCacheContext and SPICacheContext, which hold no allocations of their own. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback, citing the open feedback and concerns.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 added child contexts under CacheMemoryContext and stalled on the fragmentation they could add. This proposal also adds contexts, but on the new System context type, which has a small header and leaves allocation to malloc.

objections.title: Shared rd_supportinfo changes what support functions may cache in fn_extra
objections.failure_scenario: An extension index AM or opclass support function caches state in fn_extra, assuming it belongs to one index. After the patch, a second index with the same shape but a different collation or relation reuses that FmgrInfo. The function returns results built for the other index, or reads memory freed when the first index's relcache entry is dropped.
objections.argument: Until now each index had its own rd_supportinfo array allocated in its own rd_indexcxt, so fn_mcxt and fn_extra lived and died with one index. The shape key covers AM, key count, opclasses and opclass options, but not collation or the relation itself. Chao Li showed the fn_mcxt lifetime problem in message #4, and the author acknowledged it in message #9, but no later changelist says it was fixed. The proposal does not say which memory context owns a shared FmgrInfo or what extension authors may still put in fn_extra.
objections.author_must_show: Which context owns fn_mcxt and fn_extra for a shared rd_supportinfo in v5, and what does the patch promise extension support functions about per-index caching?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 accepts the lifetime problem, and no changelist from v2 to v5 says it is fixed or names the context that owns a shared FmgrInfo. The shape key in message #1 leaves out collation, so the fn_extra sharing question also stands.

objections.title: No numbers for the extra cost of building index relcache entries
objections.failure_scenario: A workload with many partitions runs frequent DDL or ANALYZE, and each run invalidates many index relcache entries. Every rebuild now does a shape hash lookup and every destroy does a deregistration, and SystemContext does one malloc per palloc. Users with plenty of memory see slower relcache rebuilds after upgrade and gain nothing.
objections.argument: The 0003 commit message admits extra work at load and calls it a worthy trade-off, but the thread has only memory numbers (messages #3, #22). A rebuild runs at the first access to each index in every backend and after every invalidation, so the cost falls on everyone. The memory savings help only sessions that touch many indexes.
objections.author_must_show: How much slower are backend start and relcache rebuild after mass invalidation, for example on the 148,000-index schema from message #22?

critic.reasoning: The 0003 commit message admits extra work when loading index relcache entries, and the thread has only memory numbers. Every backend pays this cost at first access and after each invalidation, so a timing measurement is a fair request.

refuted.title: Shared rd_supportinfo changes the fn_extra contract for opclass support functions
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension's opclass support function caches index-specific state in fn_extra, such as collation-dependent data, assuming one FmgrInfo per index. After upgrade, two indexes with the same opclasses but different collations share that FmgrInfo, and the second index reads state cached for the first. Nothing fails at compile time, so authors find out from wrong results.
refuted.argument: The shape key covers AM, key attribute count, opclasses and opclass options, but not rd_indcollation, which can differ between indexes. Message #1 and the 0001 commit message say rd_supportinfo is filled dynamically and so stays non-const, which means extensions get no compiler warning. The patch prose has no documentation hunk telling opclass authors that fn_extra is now shared across indexes. Message #4 raised the lifetime side of this sharing, and the material shows no fix after message #9.
refuted.author_must_show: Which core or extension support functions cache per-index or per-collation state in fn_extra, and where is the new sharing rule documented for opclass authors?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which covers the same fn_extra sharing across indexes with different collations and also the lifetime problem from message #4.

refuted.title: System contexts hide per-allocation malloc overhead in memory views
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA sums pg_backend_memory_contexts for a backend with hundreds of thousands of indexes to size per-backend memory. System contexts report requested sizes plus small headers, but malloc's own per-chunk overhead and size-class rounding stay invisible. The DBA plans memory from the view and finds out when the backend's RSS is higher than the view suggested.
refuted.argument: Existing context types malloc large blocks, so the allocator overhead the view cannot see is small relative to the totals. SystemContext issues one malloc per palloc, and the README hunk says per-allocation overhead is significant, so the unseen share grows with exactly the workloads this targets. The 776 MiB to 633 MiB result in message #22 comes from used_bytes in this view, so it may overstate the RSS saving.
refuted.author_must_show: How does backend RSS change on the 148,000-index schema, and does pg_backend_memory_contexts state that System context totals omit malloc overhead?

critic.reasoning: pg_backend_memory_contexts has never reported malloc overhead or RSS, and a System context makes only a few allocations. Message #22 compares used_bytes, which leaves out free space in aset blocks on master, so it does not overstate the saving in the way the objection describes.

refuted.title: Shared rd_supportinfo lifetime bug lets any table owner crash the server
refuted.failure_scenario: A role with CREATE on any schema makes two same-shape indexes on its own table, uses the first so its FmgrInfo is filled, then drops it. Later use of the second index can follow a freed fn_mcxt or fn_extra. A segfault makes the postmaster restart every backend, so other sessions on the cluster lose their connections.
refuted.argument: Message #4 shows that index_getprocinfo() fills the shared FmgrInfo with fn_mcxt set to one index's rd_indexcxt. Support functions may also keep fn_extra in that context, so dropping or invalidating that one index frees memory the other indexes still use. Message #9 accepted the bug and promised a fix, but the changelists for v3 and v4 (messages #25, #27) and the v5 posting (message #29) do not mention it. Creating such indexes needs only table ownership, so any unprivileged user can reach this path.
refuted.author_must_show: In v5, which context owns fn_mcxt and fn_extra of a shared rd_supportinfo, and what keeps it alive until the last index using that shape is destroyed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The crash is the same dangling fn_mcxt problem from message #4, and the privilege framing adds no separate design issue.

refuted.title: Shared rd_supportinfo changes the fmgr cache lifetime contract
refuted.failure_scenario: An opclass support function in core or an extension caches state in fn_extra, allocated in fn_mcxt, which is the first index's rd_indexcxt. That index's relcache entry is rebuilt or dropped while a sibling index still uses the shared FmgrInfo. The next call reads freed memory, and the crash depends on invalidation timing, so it is hard to reproduce.
refuted.argument: Message #4 reports the dangling fn_mcxt and fn_extra, and message #9 promises a fix. The v3 to v5 changelists (messages #25, #27, #29) do not mention one. The patch touches fmgr.h and c.h, but no commit message says what the new rule is for support functions that use fn_extra. Nothing fails loudly if a later opclass author assumes one FmgrInfo per index.
refuted.author_must_show: What owns fn_mcxt and fn_extra in a shared rd_supportinfo, and how does an opclass author learn that one FmgrInfo now serves several indexes?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same lifetime problem and the same missing rule for support functions that use fn_extra.

refuted.title: SystemContext savings depend on the platform malloc
refuted.failure_scenario: A packager builds on a libc whose malloc rounds or fragments small long-lived allocations more than glibc does. Then every "index info" and "index shape" context costs more real memory than mem_allocated reports. Users find out only when RSS grows while pg_backend_memory_contexts looks smaller.
refuted.argument: The 0005 commit message says the system allocator is "frequently" better, so the benefit rests on an allocator the project does not control. Message #3 counts context header bytes only, and the material shows no measurement on more than one platform. Message #23 also worries that extensions will use the new public API for contexts with many small allocations, and each palloc there becomes a malloc.
refuted.author_must_show: What real resident memory, not mem_allocated, does the patch save on at least two different libc malloc implementations?

critic.reasoning: Master already makes at least one malloc per "index info" context, so the patch adds no new dependence on the platform malloc. To cancel the drop from 2086 to 329 bytes per context, an allocator would have to waste far more than known size-class rounding does.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: RelationData fields become const and shared, fmgr.h and c.h change, and extensions get a new System context API.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Shared rd_supportinfo changes what support functions may cache in fn_extra

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new memory context type (systemctx.c) and a shape cache in relcache.c need care from now on.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Every index relcache build and destroy adds a shape lookup, and System contexts do one malloc per palloc.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: In v5, which memory context owns fn_mcxt and fn_extra of a shared rd_supportinfo, and what keeps it alive until the last index using that shape is destroyed?
Can a support function still cache per-index or per-collation state in fn_extra, given that the shape key does not include rd_indcollation?
How much slower are backend start and relcache rebuild after mass invalidation, for example on the 148,000-index schema from message #22?
When are shape cache entries freed under heavy relcache invalidation?
How do fmgr.h and c.h change, and what do extension authors need to adjust?

committability.owner_note: David Rowley reviewed the System context several times and sent a fixup; the deduplication patch still needs a committer who knows relcache invalidation and fmgr lifetime rules.
committability.liability: The owner signs for memory lifetime of shared FmgrInfo under relcache invalidation, a new memory context type open to extensions, and const-ified RelationData fields, for as long as the relcache keeps this layout.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted five versions over about two months, answered review quickly and kept the entry rebased.

priority.reason: Users with many partitions or indexes gain per-backend memory, with a measured drop from 776 MiB to 633 MiB in message #22. The shared rd_supportinfo ownership rule should be settled before more review of the 42 KiB deduplication patch in relcache.c and fmgr.

provisional_note: Without the code, it is not possible to check whether v5 already fixes the fn_mcxt lifetime, how the shape cache frees entries, or what the fmgr.h and c.h changes do.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE using rdtsc
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Lukas Fittl (lfittl), David Geier (geidav)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make instr_time count CPU reference cycles read with rdtsc, which does not wait for prior instructions, and convert cycles to time only on output, to cut the timing overhead of EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The patch uses rdtsc only on Linux/x86 when the kernel clocksource is tsc, takes the TSC frequency from CPUID, and falls back to clock_gettime() otherwise.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped after the v8 patch of February 2023, and nobody continued the work for about a year. vignesh C closed the entry as Returned with feedback because neither the author nor anyone else took it forward. Earlier, Andres Freund doubted the patch was ready on reliability and code complexity, citing the Linux-only restriction, but the entry closed from inactivity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the author or no one else showed interest in taking it forward
and the patch had no activity for more than 1 year, I have changed the
status to RWF.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a CONTEXT line such as "while rebuilding index qqq_a_idx" to errors raised when ALTER TABLE rebuilds indexes and constraints. It uses an error context callback, so a failure during the rebuild names the object being rebuilt.

This reverts commit d1001a78ce612a16ea622b558f5fc2b68c45ab4c of 2010-12-05,
which was broken as reported by Jeff Davis.  The problem is that the

precedents_retrieved.title: Protect syscache from bloating with negative cache entries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The first patches removed negative catcache entries through invalidation callbacks, for example when a relation or a schema is dropped. The later version adds a GUC, catalog_cache_prune_min_age, so that a backend removes catcache entries not accessed for that long when it would otherwise grow the hash table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. In the last technical messages, from January 2021, Heikki Linnakangas found the slowdown acceptable and suggested enabling the feature by default. Bruce Momjian asked in March 2021 whether it would make PG 14, and no later message is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: JIT: Optimize generated functions earlier to lower memory usage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lowers the memory used by JIT-compiled code by running the function-level LLVM optimization passes on each function as soon as it is generated. Today these passes run later, in llvm_optimize_module(), whose code comment suggests this move.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the author's opening message is shown, and the entry was withdrawn about a month later with no visible review or reply.

precedents_retrieved.title: NOTIFY and pg_notify performance when deduplicating notifications
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an optional collapse mode to NOTIFY and pg_notify(), with syntax NOTIFY channel [ , payload [ , collapse_mode ] ], so a transaction can skip the duplicate check. With 'never', notifications are queued without the O(N^2) duplicate search, so many notifications in one transaction cost linear time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to the syntax: it differs from other utility statements and needs a payload before a collapse mode can be given. He suggested NOTIFY [ (collapse = off/on) ] channel [ , payload ] and a boolean instead of the unclear 'maybe' mode. He also noted that the documentation omits 'always' mode and that the patch does not speed up duplicate notifications. The author did not post an updated patch, so Andres Freund returned it with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Shared-memory based stats collector
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace the file-based stats collector with statistics kept in dynamic shared memory (dshash), so backends read stats without a stats file written by a separate process. The stats collector process goes away, and per-kind stats code moves into new files under utils/activity.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund reworked the patch in spring 2021 and judged it not committable for v14, citing weak test coverage, the need for architectural review and performance testing, an unresolved case where stats for dropped functions can be revived, and many open FIXMEs. A rebase then stalled on a new issue with partitioned tables. No new version was posted after July 2021, so the CommitFest manager marked the entry Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Unfortunately I think
that, while it has gotten a lot closer, it's still about a week's worth of
work away from being committable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add the ability to limit the amount of memory that can be allocated to backends.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch tracks the memory each backend allocates and shows it in pg_stat_activity, and a second patch adds max_total_backend_memory to cap total backend allocations across the cluster. A later version by John Morris keeps local counters in each process and adds them to shared counters from time to time, with error of up to 1 MB per process.

roaster_notes.note: [P1] is the only related precedent, and this proposal targets its recorded concern about per-context overhead; Andres Freund, co-author of the System context, argues for more cache contexts in message #20. [P10] is about pruning catcache entries, a different idea. No earlier rejection reason applies unanswered, so I raise no objection from this angle.

The proposal adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump-visible state. The remaining user-facing changes are the new context type and context names, plus const fields that fail loudly at compile time.

The patch adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire protocol state. All shape cache state is per-backend memory and is rebuilt on restart. The only cross-boundary concern is the extension API contract for shared FmgrInfo and the const fields.

The proposal adds no SQL surface, no new privilege and no new monitoring data beyond context names and sizes in pg_backend_memory_contexts. The unbounded shape cache growth in message #24 was fixed in v3 (message #25), so it is not raised here.
Committability is reasonable. Andres Freund co-wrote SystemContext and David Rowley reviewed it closely, but the deduplication patch has had less committer review.

No existing feature or extension meets this need, because relcache allocation of opclass-derived index fields can only be changed in core. An aset context with an allocChunkLimit of zero was the obvious alternative; message #3 shows its fixed overhead is too high (200 vs 108 bytes per context), and David Rowley and Andres Freund accepted the new System context type after that answer.

The material shows real demand. David Geier reports production workloads with 10-100k tables and hundreds of thousands of indexes (message #6). On one such schema he measured relcache memory falling from 776 MiB to 633 MiB (message #22). Partitioned tables with identical index definitions are a common case that benefits (messages #8, #10). Andres Freund co-wrote the System context and wants more cache contexts made cheap (message #20). The memory saving applies per backend. The open issues are the shared rd_supportinfo lifetime and the unmeasured load cost, and both belong to other angles.
